newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent up, holds arb, but bearish signs seen.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent up, holds arb, but bearish signs seen.

text.p: June Brent crude futures in Asia edged higher in late afternoon dealings on Tuesday, maintaining its arbitrage value against NYMEX.
June Brent last traded at $17.99 per barrel, up two cents from London's close on Friday at $17.97. July was traded one cent higher at $18.15.
London and Singapore Brent markets were closed on Monday to mark a U.K. holiday.
Brokers said in the absence of clear direction from news meant the market would rely on technical factors.
They said June was looking to hold above short-term trend line support at $17.97 to retest the top end of the trading range of $17.50/$18.77.
However, some analysts said June had formed a top after failing to break above a chart gap high of $18.77. It indicated a move down to $18.61, they said.
NYMEX June crude, trading on the ACCESS system, was last traded at $19.63, flat with the New York close.
